To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prediction error is not always reduced when the number of last observed values is increased, the ARIMA model provides a better prediction than the LMMSE model, the IMS technique is more accurate than the DMS one, the granularity value at which multi-step prediction is the most accurate is different from the granularity at which the 1-step prediction is the best and that it is possible to predict the throughput of packets classified based on their size.

the ARIMA model provides the best multi-step prediction performance in the context of network traffic, and that the prediction of throughput of 1.500-byte packets is more difficult than the prediction of throughput for the other packets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the multi-step prediction performance of the ARIMA model and the LMMSE model, and the effect of some factors on the prediction error.
the study of some parameters that affect the multi-step prediction performance of the ARIMA and LMMSE models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multi-step prediction performance is highly dependent on the network environment.
ARIMA and the LMMSE model provide an acceptable performance for multi-step prediction of the traffic.
ARIMA is more appropriate for multi-step prediction of network traffic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prediction performance is not always improving when increasing the number of lags as inputs of the model.
the multi-step prediction performance depends on the number of lags, the data granularity and the packet size distribution.
the prediction of traffic based on its size is possible, however, it is less predictable than the prediction of throughput.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multi-step traffic prediction based on ARIMA model is possible and can be useful for proactive traffic engineering.
the prediction performance is highly dependent on the traffic parameters and the prediction model.
the multi-step prediction of the network traffic is possible and the IMS technique is the most appropriate for multi-step traffic prediction.
